tools.name: mcp_test_db_search_schema
tools.description: CRITICAL TOOL FOR SCHEMA EXPLORATION: Use this FIRST before writing queries. Fuzzy-searches a table name and returns its DDL plus direct parent/child table DDLs (Auto-Join Context), inferred FK hints, and semantic dictionary entries from metadata.json when configured. If templates.json is loaded, reminds you to use the 'query_templates' prompt for business metrics. Do NOT use execute_safe_query for schema exploration.

query.description: The name of the table or entity to search for (e.g. 'users', 'invoices').

tools.name: mcp_test_db_execute_safe_query
tools.description: Executes SQL against the database with AST validation. SELECT results are capped by MCP_QUERY_ROW_LIMIT (default 500, AST-injected LIMIT) and include a '-- rows: N (truncated at LIMIT X)' footer when the cap is reached. Unindexed full table scans above MCP_EXPLAIN_MAX_SCAN_ROWS are blocked before execution. Write operations (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL) are enabled; UPDATE and DELETE require a WHERE clause. Only the configured schema is reachable: SHOW statements, information_schema/mysql/performance_schema/sys, other schemas, server variables, SELECT ... INTO and functions such as LOAD_FILE or SLEEP are rejected by the server. To explore the schema use 'search_schema'.

sql.description: SQL statement to execute. SELECT is always allowed; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL only when enabled in server config. UPDATE and DELETE must include a WHERE clause.

tools.name: mcp_test_db_refresh_schema
tools.description: Rebuilds the internal Schema Graph from the live database and notifies subscribed MCP resources. Use when search_schema or execute_safe_query fail with missing table/column errors after a schema change.

tools.name: mcp_test_db_ping
tools.description: Health check: verifies the database connection is alive. Returns JSON with status, MySQL server version, and connection pool stats (active, idle, queued).

status.description: Whether the database connection is healthy

queue.description: Queued requests waiting for a connection

tools.name: mcp_test_db_explain_query
tools.description: Returns MySQL EXPLAIN output as CSV for a validated SELECT query. SQL is AST-validated and timeout-protected; ANALYZE and non-SELECT statements are blocked. Unlike execute_safe_query, this does NOT block full table scans — use it to diagnose why a query was blocked or to verify index usage before executing.

select_type.description: Type of SELECT (SIMPLE, PRIMARY, SUBQUERY, etc.)

type.description: Join type (ALL, index, range, ref, const, etc.)

prompts.name: mcp_test_db_query_templates
prompts.description: Returns pre-approved SQL templates for business metrics (requires templates.json via MCP_TEMPLATES_PATH). Use before writing analytical SQL from scratch. Execute the returned SQL via execute_safe_query.

arguments.name: query
arguments.description: Keyword to search for in templates (e.g., 'revenue', 'ltv').

resources.name: schema
resources.description: Lists all available tables in the database schema

resourceTemplates.name: table
resourceTemplates.description: Exposes the SQL DDL and semantic dictionary of a specific table

  `total` decimal(10,2) DEFAULT NULL,
  `currency` varchar(3) DEFAULT 'USD',
  `payment_method` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,

--- PRE-APPROVED SQL TEMPLATES ---

### Customer Lifetime Value (LTV)
Description: Calculates the total revenue generated by each customer across all delivered orders. Use this whenever asked for LTV.
SQL:
```sql
SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) as ltv FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY ltv DESC
```

### Product Performance (Total Sales)
Description: Calculates the total quantity sold and revenue generated per product. Use this for 'best selling products' or 'product revenue'.
SQL:
```sql
SELECT p.id, p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_units_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) as total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status != 'pending' GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
```
